baselineFindings.finding: The community domain persists communities, deletion markers, events and audit records in localStorage, so browser state can manufacture membership, roles, discipline and governance outcomes.
Discovery uses a mock-data service while the internal community experience uses a separate local browser domain, creating multiple non-canonical sources for the same community identity.

Authenticated browser sessions can directly insert or mutate communities, memberships and posts through table grants and RLS; no server-owned command, idempotent acknowledgement or durable outbox boundary exists.
The remote model has no canonical invitations, private join requests, approval lifecycle, invitation expiry, request replay or server-audited membership decision contract.
The database accepts only owner, moderator and member while the browser supports custom roles and granular permissions, so authorization semantics diverge across devices and enforcement layers.
Bans, mutes, restrictions, channel discipline and reasons are browser-local and can be edited or removed without a canonical server case, immutable event chain or expiry worker.
Members insert posts directly as published and authors can update title and body directly; no moderation intake, content revision ledger, text safety, rate limit or report linkage is authoritative.
No community realtime publication, channel subscription authorization, fan-out policy, presence boundary or scalable channel lifecycle is active.
Channels, announcement restrictions, slow mode, link blocking, pinned messages and community chat exist only in the browser domain and have no remote schema or server authority.
The generic reports table does not define community-specific target validation, sanction state, restoration, appeal, evidence retention, operator separation or dual-control rules.
The local domain merges account IDs, profile IDs and email aliases into browser-derived identity keys, which is not a canonical authenticated subject boundary.
No authoritative upload validation, malware scanning, media moderation, retention, deletion, CDN or appeal boundary exists for community content.

mandatoryInvariants: authenticated UUID sessions never create authoritative community state in localStorage
community discovery uses one canonical projection with explicit public private and unavailable states
community creation and mutation use server-owned commands with stable client request identity
private communities are not enumerable by nonmembers
invitations and join requests have canonical identity expiry status and idempotency
membership decisions are concurrency-safe and auditable
the canonical owner membership cannot be deleted downgraded or reassigned implicitly
custom roles and permissions are versioned server-side and cannot exceed the acting role authority
members cannot self-promote or grant permissions they do not possess
bans mutes restrictions and channel discipline use canonical cases with reason actor expiry and revision
sanction expiry and restoration are deterministic and audited
posts and messages enter an explicit content lifecycle rather than client-selected publication
content revisions reports removals restorations and appeals are append-only and auditable
community realtime subscriptions are scoped by canonical membership and channel access
slow mode rate limits link restrictions and channel send rules are enforced server-side
lost-response retries return the same membership post message or moderation outcome
raw credentials identity documents payment data and private unrelated messages are prohibited from community audit events
community media uses validated private upload authority moderation and retention rules
local fixtures and caches never create production community or moderation authority
